contributions.headingText: Odontogenic carcinosarcoma is a malignant mixed odontogenic tumour in which the epithelial component and the ectomesenchymal component show features of malignancy.
2B5J & XH4LP1 Malignant miscellaneous tumours of bone or articular cartilage of other or unspecified sites & Odontogenic carcinosarcoma
Not recommended: malignant odontogenic mixed tumour; ameloblastic carcinosarcoma.
All cases have involved the posterior mandible, with 1 equivocal case in the maxilla {1987921; 30554629}.

Most patients present with pain and swelling. The mean tumour diameter at diagnosis is approximately 60 mm. Paraesthesia or anaesthesia has been reported.

Imaging

Radiographically, most patients present with highly destructive, poorly marginated radiolucencies. Cortical perforation is common, followed by soft tissue extension {26131431}.

Cases have been reported from Japan, Saudi Arabia, the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, the Republic of Korea, France, Germany, Brazil, and the USA. Age incidence has not been defined, although the mean age of female patients is significantly lower than that of male patients. There are twice as many male patients as female patients {30220320}.
Most cases have been associated with a previously existing odontogenic neoplasm, often ameloblastic fibroma or ameloblastic fibrosarcoma {17395065; 30220320}.
The neoplasm is often tan, lobulated, and fleshy {17395065; 21195529}.

Histopathological features are based on few cases, but they resemble those of ameloblastic fibroma or fibrosarcoma. Both the epithelial and ectomesenchymal components must show convincing cytological features of malignancy. The epithelial component ranges from fine strands to larger islands, often with peripheral palisading. The ectomesenchymal component is hypercellular with cytological atypia. Mesenchymal hard tissues such as dentinoid, bone, and cartilage may be produced, but the histological appearances do not mimic osteosarcoma or other defined sarcomas. Both components show a high mitotic count and Ki-67 proliferative index {17395065; 30554629}.

Immunohistochemistry

The epithelial component is reactive for a variety of cytokeratins, particularly CK19. The ectomesenchymal component is invariably positive for vimentin but may also show reactivity for desmin and MSA {30554629}.

Differential diagnosis

This must exclude a malignant epithelial odontogenic tumour with a spindle cell component of epithelial origin, such as ameloblastic carcinoma, a significant diagnostic pitfall {30928327}. The formation of matrix or hard tissue in an odontogenic carcinoma does not necessarily indicate sarcoma {11903826; 25409850}. A spindle cell squamous carcinoma usually demonstrates epithelial differentiation histologically and/or immunohistochemically.

Essential: origin in a tooth-bearing segment of the jaws; carcinoma and sarcoma components; significant cytological atypia in both components; exclusion of spindle cell squamous carcinoma.

Desirable: evidence of a pre-existing odontogenic tumour.

Although there is no defined eighth-edition Union for International Cancer Control (UICC) / American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) TNM staging system staging guidance, the use of International Collaboration on Cancer Reporting (ICCR) minimum data set reporting is encouraged {30500289}.

The treatment of choice is wide surgical excision. Almost two thirds of patients experience recurrence and just over 40% have metastasis, most often to lung. Disease-associated mortality is about 50% {30220320}.
